title: Telemetry-led bandit kernel explorer + prefill/decoder smoother
creator: Avery Cho
description: Spike + implementation ticket to explore a telemetry-driven, bandit-style kernel-selection optimizer and a complementary prefill->decode smoothing layer. Goal: reduce p95 tail regressions when introducing FlashAttention v3 kernels for mixed workloads while preserving cost gains. Deliverables: (1) lightweight bandit controller that adjusts kernel weights per workload fingerprint and context-length bucket, (2) prefill/decoder smoothing shim that staggers kernel switching during startup and burst scenarios, (3) telemetry schema and dashboards to validate behavioral drift and safe rollback hooks, (4) controlled rollout plan with canary and fast rollback. Rationale: recent integrations of FlashAttention v3 show improved median latency but several customers and internal benchmarks report decode jitter and occasional workspace OOMs at higher concurrency. A purely static kernel routing table leads to thrashing under bursty prefill-decode patterns. The proposed approach continuously scores kernels by a latency+stability reward and decays exploration over time. The smoothing shim prevents immediate handoffs during the first N tokens and coordinates warmup buffers to avoid oscillation between v2/v3 on the same connection.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Triage: summarized problem from customer incident #INC-5732 (dropped to eng). Decided to scope as performance/regression mitigation rather than full kernel rewrite.

2026-03-02 — Spike: implemented a PoC bandit controller inside runtime dev env (local harness). Algorithm: epsilon-greedy per (model, seq_bucket) with decay. Observed 6% p95 reduction on webtext-lm workload vs static routing but p99 unchanged. Noted single-model edge-case for 8k context where v3 workspace allocation spikes.

2026-03-03 — Telemetry spec reviewed by SRE (Maria Gonzalez). Added metrics: kernel_choice, kernel_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), workspace_peak_mb, workspace_failure_count, decode_jitter_ms, warmup_switch_count. Added tags: model_name, context_bucket, route_key, instance_type.

2026-03-04 — Design review with Runtime/Infra: agreed to add a smoothing shim that enforces a minimal grace_tokens window (default 64) before allowing a kernel handoff, plus a cooldown period after a failure. Trade-offs: slightly higher median on short prompts vs stability at tail. PM (Jordan Lee) requested cost impact estimate for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-04 — Dev note: opened PR runtime/pull/4281 with bandit controller and runtime flag --kernel-explorer. Includes unit tests and simulation harness reading historical telemetry to bootstrap priors.

2026-03-05 — Canary plan: 1% of hosted API traffic -> explorer enabled, split across three model families (gpt-compat-small, redwood/open-llama-7b, fastformer-xl). Monitor: kernel_failure_rate<0.1%, decode_jitter delta < 10ms. If workspace_failure_count increases by >50% in any shard we auto-disable.

Follow-ups: add A/B analysis dashboard (Perf->Kernel Explorer) and a rollback automation ticket in ops if canary triggers. Also need an RFC for per-tenant opt-out and dedicated contract implications (Samir to loop Legal/Enterprise Sales).
